transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. No — do not buy or use a DIY regas kit. A sealed-system engineer should assess that side. With both the freezer and fridge warm despite the compressor running, low refrigerant is one possibility, but it is not proven by that alone. A dirty condenser/grille, poor ventilation, an incorrect setting or restricted airflow can also prevent proper cooling. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Vacuum dust gently from the rear/underneath grille or coils, and make sure it is not tight against the wall or enclosed with no airflow. Heavy dust or no clearance can make it run but fail to cool.
2. Check the controls are set normally — roughly 3–5°C for the fridge and -18°C for the freezer — and that holiday/eco mode is not selected.
3. Make sure internal air vents are not covered by food or heavy ice. Keep the doors shut as much as possible afterwards, then allow several hours to see whether it begins cooling. If it remains warm after those checks while the compressor continues to run, a sealed cooling-system fault or compressor/control issue becomes more likely and needs an engineer rather than a regas kit.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

ive checked the back already, its only barely warm, not hot like it used to be. thermostat is on normal. compressor just hums non stop. so is it the gas then or not? and whats the cheapest way to sort it, its out of warranty

It could be the gas circuit, but those symptoms do not prove it is simply “low on gas”. With both sections warm, the compressor humming continuously, and the back now only barely warm, the leading possibilities are a sealed-system fault (leak or restriction) or a compressor that is running but no longer pumping properly. A start relay fault is less likely if it genuinely hums continuously rather than humming, clicking off, then trying again every few minutes. If refrigerant is low, there is normally a leak or another fault to find and repair first; adding gas alone may cool briefly but will not be a lasting repair. Ask for a diagnosis and quote before authorising sealed-system work, as a compressor or major leak repair can sometimes be poor value on an out-of-warranty fridge-freezer. One useful no-tools check: look at the rear wall inside the freezer after it has been running for a while. Any frost/ice there, versus no frost at all, helps separate an airflow/defrost issue from a cooling-circuit or compressor problem. Do not remove panels or disturb any pipes.
no frost anywhere in the freezer, the back wall isnt even cold. freezer is about 0C now and everything has thawed. there is a fan going when the door is shut. so whats that mean?

That points away from a defrost or fan problem. The fan is running, but there is no frost and the freezer back is not cold, so the appliance is not producing cooling in the first place. The most likely causes are, in order:
1. A fault in the sealed cooling circuit — often a refrigerant leak or a restriction.
2. A compressor that runs continuously but is no longer pumping effectively. So, it may be “the gas”, but it is not safe or accurate to assume it merely needs topping up. Refrigerant does not get used up; if it is low, there is usually a leak that needs finding and repairing first. There is no further owner-safe check that can reliably separate a leak/restriction from a weak compressor. That needs a refrigeration engineer’s test equipment and must be done on the sealed system. For the cheapest sensible route, ask an independent refrigeration/appliance engineer for a fixed-price diagnosis, specifically saying: both compartments are warm, compressor hums continuously, freezer is around 0°C, fan runs, no frost/cold rear freezer wall, and the condenser area is only barely warm. Ask for the diagnosis and total repair quote before approving work. If it is a compressor replacement or an inaccessible leak, replacement is often better value on an out-of-warranty fridge-freezer. Move any remaining food elsewhere and avoid relying on it for chilled or frozen food.
